requires_in_meal.note: Qubus is only ever served with grilled chicken or grilled fish - never with Indian dishes.
Hummus is a grilled-plate accompaniment, never served with Indian dishes.
Same as hummus - only on the grilled plate.
Plain curd belongs with the parathas.

plate_rules.note: Grilled plate: qubus + grilled chicken + hummus or garlic paste + salad. Never an Indian curry.
Parathas are eaten with plain curd only - never rasam, kadala curry or any other curry.
Same as methi paratha - plain curd only.

batter_notes: These ferment overnight. The same one is served two days running (one batter, two days), and two DIFFERENT batter dishes must never fall on consecutive days. The user may override by hand.

rules.repetition_notes: This family repeats dishes through the week (batch cooking; dosa/idli/appam batter lasts ~2 days so the same batter dish can appear on two days with different sides; a lunch fish curry can also be that day's dinner curry). Do NOT force variety.

placement.rice_only_note: Thin, soupy curries that are poured over rice. They never go with chapati, puri or any other bread. Matched on the name, so 'Tomato Rasam' counts as Rasam.
placement.no_consecutive_days_note: Fish Fry is deliberately NOT here - it may repeat on back-to-back days.
placement.grilled_chicken_days: ONLY Friday or Saturday dinner, never mid-week

grocery.exclude_from_list: spices, masalas, condiments (turmeric, mustard seeds, chili powder, garam masala, etc.) - the family always has these
grocery.fruits: list individual fruit items as an editable list, NOT a single 'fruits for the week' line

_notes.seafood_rule: fish and prawns share the same conflicts (curd/yogurt/buttermilk/moru/pachadi/curd rice, bitter gourd, milk). Both are listed explicitly so a simple keyword match works.
_notes.incompatible_dish_pairs: Dish-name-level conflicts that the ingredient rule can't catch. Fish Curry + Fish Fry are both 'fish' so they never trigger the ingredient list; they must be one-or-the-other via this list. Same for Sambar + Avial (too much prep + overlapping vegetables).
_notes.required_pairings: A dish must be served with one of its listed partners. 'any curry' means any recipe whose component is 'curry'.
_notes.avial: Avial no longer uses curd in this database, so it does NOT trigger the fish/prawns conflict.
_notes.frequency_field: Optional field on a recipe. 'rare' = serve roughly once every 1-2 months (e.g. Mutton Biryani). Omit for regular dishes.
_notes.serves_subset_field: Optional boolean. true = only one or two family members eat this (e.g. Pasta); the meal planner should schedule a parallel main for everyone else on that day.
_notes.day_preference_field: Optional field. 'weekend' = usually served on weekends only (e.g. Puri). Omit for any-day dishes.
_notes.also_meal_types_field: Optional array. Extra meal slots a dish also fits beyond its primary meal_type (e.g. Pav Bhaji: meal_type 'dinner', also_meal_types ['breakfast']).
